text:
kevin: Heads-up — last night's benchmark alert for runtime/nightly triggered a p99 regression vs baseline. Suspect KV-cache warmup + shorter synthetic prefixes. Starting a quick triage thread.

ci-bot: nightly-bench job #482 failed: p99 +12% (vs baseline). Attached artifacts: s3://bench-artifacts/nightly/482 (replay logs, flamegraphs).

maria: saw the same in the apples-to-apples run. The replay shows a LOT more cache misses in the first 50 tokens. synthetic traffic uses short prompts which doesn't warm kv-cache.

alex: can we repro by running the replay harness with longer prefixes? I can run 5 replays locally.

dave: I pulled the flamegraph — kernel selector seems to fallback to slower attention kernel on a subset of steps when seq_len spikes. That + cold kv cache explains the latency tail.

maria: agree. Also our alert currently compares single nightly run to baseline with a hard 10% p99 threshold. That's brittle for cache-warmup-sensitive workloads.

kevin: proposal: change alerting to require either (a) 3 consecutive failing nights OR (b) median-of-5 nightly runs > threshold. Also add a replay flag to the CI job to force kv warmup so apples-to-apples.

dave: +1. Suggested alert rule (pseudo):
```json
{
  "metric": "p99_latency_ms",
  "window": "7d",
  "require": "count(fails) >= 3 || median(runs,5) > 1.10 * baseline"
}
```

maria: also suggest increasing replay sample size in CI: run `replay-harness --mode apples-to-apples --replays 5 --kv-warmup true` so the noise from first-token misses is averaged out.

alex: I'll add that to the nightly job config and run 10 local replays to validate. Command I'm going to run: 
```
./tools/replay-harness --workload prod-replay --seed 42 --replays 10 --kv-warmup
```
I'll paste results here when done. :eyes:

ci-bot: scheduled nightly-bench (job #483) with updated flags: `--replays 5 --kv-warmup` (pending run).

srebot: muting alert channel for nightly-bench until we roll the new alert rule. Will keep a pinned incident thread. :white_check_mark:

kevin: action items:
- alex: update nightly job + run 10 local replays and share plots (ETA today)
- maria: draft alert-rule PR to use median-of-5 or 3-run confirmation (ETA tomorrow)
- dave: dig into kernel-selector logs to see why fallback happened for those steps (ETA EOD)
- ops (srebot/ci-bot): mute noisy alert until PR merges + validate next nightly (job #483)

maria: one more note — we should include a small kv-cache warmup synthetic phase in our apples-to-apples harness so we don't depend on random prompt lengths. I can add that as `--kv-warmup-bytes 1024`.

alex: ack. will include warmup and add a `--perf-seed` to make runs deterministic.

dave: if kernel fallback persists after warmup, we should add a tiny micro-benchmark in CI exercising the new kernel path so regressions show up faster.

kevin: sounds good. Thanks all — keep this thread updated with links to PRs and the next nightly run. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: job #483 finished: p99 delta +1.2% (within new median-of-5 tolerance). Artifacts: s3://bench-artifacts/nightly/483.

alex: uploaded run logs + per-run p99 CSV: s3://bench-artifacts/nightly/483/runs.csv — variance down after warmup flag and median-of-5. Will open a follow-up ticket for kernel selector telemetry.

maria: PR #789 opened: alert rule + CI flags. Please review.

dave: found kernel-selector corner case (quantized kernels misclassified when seq_len==64 and batch_mix high) — created draft fix, will bench.

kevin: excellent. We'll close the noisy alert once PR lands and deploy pipeline. Thanks everyone.
